look: XORA site look, same as the V00 welcome film: deep void ground, frosted glass panels with thin cyan-to-violet edges, fictional market lines drawing in, calm eased motion, the brain tutor guiding from the bottom-right corner

scenes.name: Lesson three
scenes.desc: Title card: Phase 1, lesson T03, Trading pairs: BTC/USDT; the tutor walks in.

scenes.name: Price tags
scenes.desc: A shop price tag compares money with one unit of an item; a BTC price compares USDT with one BTC.

scenes.name: Two halves
scenes.desc: Trading pair defined; BTC/USDT splits into the base asset BTC and the quote asset USDT.

scenes.name: Symbols
scenes.desc: Symbol defined: BTC/USDT and BTCUSDT are the same pair; read the price as USDT per one BTC.

scenes.name: USDT, a stablecoin
scenes.desc: Stablecoin defined: USDT is designed to stay near 1 US dollar while BTC swings; a measuring stick.

scenes.name: Quantity
scenes.desc: Quantity defined: one BTC as 1,000 pieces; 0.001 BTC is worth 60 USDT at 60,000 USDT per BTC.

scenes.name: Notional value
scenes.desc: Notional value defined; worked example 0.05 BTC x 60,000 USDT per BTC = 3,000 USDT.

scenes.name: Watch it update
scenes.desc: A calculator updates as the price moves: 1 BTC and 0.001 BTC at 60,000, 63,000 and 57,000 USDT.

scenes.name: You do not need 60,000
scenes.desc: Common mistake: thinking you need 60,000 USDT; you choose the quantity, 0.001 BTC costs 60 USDT.

scenes.name: Try it
scenes.desc: Pause and calculate: 0.02 BTC at 65,000 USDT per BTC is 1,300 USDT.

scenes.name: Other pairs
scenes.desc: ETH/USDT at 3,000 and ETH/BTC at 0.05: the quote asset can be something other than USDT.

scenes.name: Stablecoin risks
scenes.desc: A stablecoin can lose its peg, depends on its issuer and reserves; notional value is not profit.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Three key points and one question to check yourself.

scenes.name: Up next
scenes.desc: End card: next lesson T04, What does an exchange do?
